architecture_decisions: 5.1 Structural success and acceptance verification are separate facts
work_items: 5.2 The admissible evidence mode is derived from durable PLAN authority
validations: 5.2 The admissible evidence mode is derived from durable PLAN authority

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Tests and authoritative records identify the exact existing behavior: the static-web validator is structural, while autonomy currently stamps the complete acceptance map into TEST/VERIFY `acceptance_ids_verified` and the runtime-evidence adapter assumes that field represents all TEST/VERIFY acceptance coverage.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A production-shaped PLAN-bound static-web run with successful TEST records scope `STRUCTURAL_ONLY`, all protected IDs as targeted/unverified, and an empty verified list.
AC-03: validate protected requirement — The same exact evidence partition is required for successful VERIFY.
AC-04: validate protected requirement — Tests prove missing, malformed, partial, drifted or non-static PLAN execution-contract identity cannot authorize the structural-only envelope.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Tests prove a non-static run or direct protected-stage call that supplies `STRUCTURAL_ONLY` / `static-web-v1` fields without an exact resolved static-web PLAN identity fails closed.
AC-06: validate protected requirement — Tests reject duplicate, omitted, added or overlapping verified/unverified/targeted IDs and reject any scope value other than the fixed server value.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Existing full-verification paths continue to require `acceptance_ids_verified` to exactly match the protected acceptance map and existing regressions remain green.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — A fully successful structural static-web BUILD/TEST/VERIFY sequence reaches REVIEW, not FAILED or COMPLETE, with explicit unverified acceptance evidence and the existing REVIEW-required event/stop semantics.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Existing review validation still requires recommendation PASS, exact all acceptance IDs verified and the current implementation workspace digest. Structural TEST/VERIFY evidence alone cannot complete REVIEW.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The runtime-evidence adapter accepts exact full-verification and exact structural-only TEST/VERIFY envelopes as distinct modes, rejects malformed/mixed envelopes, binds the mode and exact acceptance partition into stage digests, and does not emit a behavioral-acceptance claim from structural-only evidence.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Protected attempt projection safely exposes structural scope and targeted/verified/unverified IDs while existing secret/private-reasoning/provider-payload guards remain intact. Run-event metadata need not duplicate those facts.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Diff review proves no command, validation profile, execution-contract digest, provider/model/credential/network, source-lineage, Git/Preview, merge, retry, lifecycle, REVIEW-completion or production authority increase.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Spec validation, authentic DSPy SpecCritic/SpecCompiler, strict DSPy plan validation, focused tests, full API regression, Bounded Autonomy, Workstream Spec Validation and P2 CI pass on exact reviewed heads.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — Exact merged source reaches production READY; normal production preflights pass; canonical `/health` and `/ready` return HTTP 200; exact-deployment runtime scans are clean.

AC-15: validate protected requirement — After deployment, a safe new static-web run or bounded production-shaped replay proves successful structural TEST/VERIFY no longer records every acceptance criterion as verified, downstream evidence preserves the structural-only scope, and the run still stops at human REVIEW.

critique: The current implementation of the `static-web-v1` application fails to meet the requirements for a successful static-web run. Specifically, it fails to ensure that the immutable server-owned static-web command completed successfully against the exact accepted source lineage. The current implementation does not provide a durable PLAN authority that can independently inspect the latest passed PLAN attempt for the run, parse the `ExecutionContractIdentity`, resolve it through the existing closed server catalog, and require exact identity equality. This results in the run reaching the `static-web-v1` boundary without being able to produce the desired behavior.
